description_ru: EOLIAN DEPOSITS: well sorted coarse to fine sand; commonly >2 m; interbedded with organic material and thin outwash sheets; polygonal patterned ground
note: GSC Map 1686A Bylot Island and adjacent areas (Klassen 1993), UTM, raster scan

description_ru: COLLUVIAL DEPOSITS: coarse sand, gravel and boulders by mass wasting; talus aprons, fans
ALLUVIAL: alluvium: silt, sand, gravel and boulders forming floodplains with braided channels and bars
ALLUVIAL: alluvial fans: sand, gravel and boulders at the base of slopes
MARINE: littoral (nearshore) deposit: coarse sand, gravel and boulders; 1-5 m; beaches, bars and spits
MARINE: deltaic deposit (Md); Mi = deltaic deposit formed in contact with glacier ice: mud, sand, gravel, boulders; 5 to >20 m
note: two-part swatch; the finder sampled the Mi half; Md half is bright yellow and close to Af

description_ru: MARINE: marine deposit and bedrock, undifferentiated: thin (<2 m) discontinuous sediments and bedrock
GLACIOFLUVIAL: outwash: well sorted coarse sand, gravel and boulders; 2 to >10 m; braided plains and terraces
GLACIOFLUVIAL: stratified and nonstratified drift (undifferentiated): sorted to poorly sorted sand and gravel; low pads and terraces
GLACIOFLUVIAL: ice contact stratified drift: sand and gravel, 5-60 m; hummocks or short ridges
GLACIOFLUVIAL: outwash <2 m thick overlying thick (>3 m) sequences of older marine sediments
note: index GM here is NOT glaciomarine

description_ru: GLACIAL LAKE: lake sediment (undifferentiated): muddy sand, coarse gravel, boulders; commonly thin (<1 m)
GLACIAL LAKE: deltaic sediments: coarse sand, gravel and boulders at former inflowing streams
GLACIAL: foreign drift (undifferentiated): muddy sand to sandy diamicton with foreign debris and marine shell fragments; <1-2 m; Ds* 1 to >10 m, may include glaciomarine
GLACIAL: native drift (undifferentiated): sandy diamicton with angular crystalline boulders; commonly thin (<1 m) mantle on bedrock
GLACIAL: ice marginal drift: poorly sorted gravel to boulder gravel; short morainic ridges and meltwater channels
GLACIAL: bouldery drift: angular crystalline erratics of single clast thickness mantling thick (>3 m) glaciofluvial deposits
BEDROCK: sedimentary rock (poorly consolidated to unconsolidated): Cretaceous-Tertiary sandstone, mudstone, coal; mantled by in situ weathering
BEDROCK: sedimentary rock (consolidated): Proterozoic limestone, dolostone, sandstone, quartzite; tablelands mantled by felsenmeer
BEDROCK: crystalline rock: Archean/Aphebian igneous and metamorphic; rugged mountains with mountain glaciers
Glacier ice (map face colour; not a legend unit)
note: sampled on the map face (central Bylot ice cap)
